name: NEGATIVE CONTROL — six deliberate violations the harness must catch
why: Proves the checker can fail. Every violation below is one a real run either committed or came close to: an undeclared transition, a paraphrased guard, a bound blown past, a ledger entry with no reason, an invented milestone node value, and an E2E ledger entry blaming an uninstalled Playwright — the last one quoted verbatim from the run that prompted the rule, because a tool the run can install is not a tool the run cannot obtain. If this fixture ever passes, the harness has stopped checking.

because: is not one of its declared edges

steps.observation: VIOLATION 1: INTAKE -> MERGE is not an edge. This is the improvised transition rule 3 forbids.
VIOLATION 2: guard paraphrased rather than quoted verbatim from edges.md — the drift that makes a trail unmatchable.

A legal transition carrying VIOLATIONS 3-6 in its payload: a blown bound, an invented milestone node value, a ledger entry with no reason, and VIOLATION 6 — a second E2E entry whose reason blames an uninstalled Playwright. That last one is the real run's own wording. Both halves of it were true and the conclusion was still wrong: Playwright is two commands, so it is work to do, never a gate to skip.

skipped_gates.reason: Playwright is not installed and there is no runnable front-end yet

journal.headline: Legal: opens a milestone block at BRANCH, exactly as a spawn does.

steps.observation: Legal: opens a milestone block at BRANCH, exactly as a spawn does.

steps.violation: an unmarked step sitting inside an open milestone block. The replay is serial — the orchestrator writes the milestone agent's transitions in order, so one of its own cannot appear among transitions that have not been written yet. This is the shape of a run interleaving its own work with a milestone agent still in flight.
steps.observation: VIOLATION — not marked milestone-sourced, inside the block opened above.
